name: BBC concurrent codes: two messages in one codeword
why: The plugin boundary end to end (ADR-0028) and the property the codec is named for. A BBC codeword is a Z channel: marks are set by any message and cleared by none, so several messages superimpose as a bitwise OR and all of them decode back out. A decoder that returns the first message and stops passes every single-message test there is, which is why this asserts both. It is also the only fixture whose chain ends in a browser plugin rather than a native node or an external program, so it is what proves the harness can reach one at all — the reason this decoder went without a fixture was that it could not.

expect.note: Two records, in the order the tree walk reaches them. The count is the assertion: one record means the concurrent property has been lost somewhere, and one record is exactly what a plausible-looking regression produces.

note: The codeword is 96% zeros, so the NRZ slicer has to hold a symbol clock through runs of two hundred idle bit periods. It manages because the symbol estimator scores every run as a whole number of symbols rather than assuming the shortest run is one symbol — the rewrite that fixtures/fhss-6ch forced. Revert that and this fixture is one of the places it shows.
